packageRules.description: The folder sources of the platform Applications point at this repo: a git-tags dep with targetRevision main that can never update, so it would only sit in the dashboard as invalid-value
The Cilium chart is pinned twice (cilium_chart_version in infra/env.hcl and the hubble-ui app); the UI must match the deployed chart, so bump both in one branch.

agent-sandbox is a git-sourced chart pinned twice: its targetRevision comes from the argocd manager's git-tags lookup, its image.tag from the regex docker lookup. Neither datasource reports a release timestamp (git-tags has none; docker does only on Docker Hub), so minimumReleaseAgeBehaviour=timestamp-optional let both skip the 3-day gate and git-tags offered the v1.0.8 tag while upstream had no v1.0.8 release. github-releases only offers published releases and carries published_at; the tag's images are promoted before the release is published, so image.tag still names a real image. Only packageName+datasource are overridden, never the depName: branch-time auto-replace re-extracts the file with each manager's raw depName, so an overrideDepName mismatches it and fails the branch update.
The chart index gives no source URL, so Renovate fetches no release notes into the PR body. Upstream tags the chart v4.13.x, so the changelog lookup resolves.

An OCI chart artifact carries no source URL either, so its release notes are never fetched. The oci:// repoURL resolves through the docker datasource (argocd manager), so no matchDatasources filter: the package name is unique, and matching it alone survives a manager-side datasource change. Upstream tags it v0.8.x, matching the chart version.

A sourceUrl rule cannot fetch the seaweedfs chart's release notes: upstream (same repo as the chart) tags releases 4.51, and Renovate matches release notes to the new version by exact tag string, which never equals the chart index 4.51.0. Track the releases instead, as agent-sandbox does, and the tag is the version: the release notes and the rewrite value both come out of the release list. loose versioning is required because the semver scheme rejects two-segment tags (isVersion 4.51 is false under it); loose compares them fine (4.49.0 -> 4.51). Renovate then rewrites the pin to the release tag, e.g. 4.49.0 -> 4.51; the chart is published within a day of each release, so the 3-day minimumReleaseAge gate sees chart versions that exist. Never override the depName: branch-time auto-replace re-extracts the file with the raw manager depName (see the agent-sandbox rule). registryUrls is required because the dep inherits the chart index URL (seaweedfs.github.io) from the argocd extract and overrideDatasource does not clear it — the github-releases GraphQL then POSTs to .../helm/api/graphql and 405s (agent-sandbox never saw this because git-tags carries no registryUrls). Tag inventory verified: modern releases are all 4.NN; the two lettered ancient tags version below the current pin and can never be proposed.
Hold the CI Python at 3.14: ansible-core (latest 2.21.5) supports up to 3.14, and the pre-commit ansible-lint hook crashes on 3.15. Lift the cap once ansible-core supports 3.15.

Automerge routine updates 3 days after release when the datasource reports a release timestamp: docker outside Docker Hub and git-tags carry none, and the default timestamp-required would hold every branch containing them pending forever.

Hold minor and major bumps for a human: patch and digest automerge, but anything that can change behaviour waits for a merge click and gets the label that starts the breaking-change analysis. After the age rule on purpose: a later packageRule wins, and this one must not be undone by its automerge: true.

Hold every Talos bump for a human, patches included: `cluster` upgrades all four nodes in place behind a fixed 5-minute per-node drain (`nodedrain.DefaultDrainTimeout`, not configurable from the `talos_machine` resource), so an unattended apply is a cluster-wide operation on a timer. The 2026-10-30 v1.14.4->v1.14.5 patch bump was auto-applied, wedged on two worker drains and left both cordoned; `needs-review` makes `renovate-atlantis-apply.py` refuse it so the apply waits for a chosen window.
Atlantis is the sole merger for infra PRs (apply-before-merge)
CLI versions pinned in several files (CI, the Atlantis initConfig script, the windrunner playbook) must move in one branch
CLI versions pinned in several files (CI, the Atlantis initConfig script, the windrunner setup script) must move in one branch
Every kubectl and kubernetes_version pin must move in one branch so they never disagree
The k3s install must track kubernetes_version in infra/env.hcl

The self-hosted image and the pre-commit validator rev are the same Renovate release stream; bump both in one branch. Must stay below the file-based group rules, which set groupName for .github/** and .pre-commit-config.yaml and win by being later. minimumReleaseAge is off for the pair because only the hook reports a release timestamp: the 3-day gate would hold it back while the image (no timestamp, timestamp-optional) ran ahead, leaving the engine and its validator on different versions.
